subject: Post-call: inference parity vs hyperscalers — proposed tests & next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>

Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call recap & proposed test matrix (parity vs hyperscalers)

Hi Sara — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a concrete set of next steps so we can run a tight competitive evaluation against the hyperscalers.

Key takeaways from call:
- Your priorities: deterministic tail latency for chat features, reliable tool/function-calling for automated workflows, and structured outputs for ingestion into ML pipelines.
- Current comparison set: AWS Bedrock + managed LLMs, Google Vertex, and an existing self-hosted endpoint. You called out streaming reliability and function-calling parity as gating items.

What Redwood offers (high level):
- Serving runtime optimized for streaming (SSE + chunked frames) with predictable per-token latency under load.
- First-class function/tool-calling: typed function schemas, retries, and canonical fallback when external tool fails.
- Structured-output support: validators for JSON Schema and optional post-processing hooks to enforce shape.
- Cost & performance levers: continuous batching, KV prefix caching, and quantization profiles to reduce per-token cost without retraining.

Proposed evaluation tests (we recommend running these in parallel):
1) Streaming stability & tail-latency test (S1): 10k generated tokens per minute across 5 concurrency levels, measure p50/p95/p99 and reconnect behavior.
2) Tool/function-calling parity (T1): 6 canonical flows invoking an internal API (info lookup, ticket create, payment check) — verify payload integrity, retries, and edge-case handling.
3) Structured outputs (J1): JSON Schema-constrained outputs for 20 prompt variants; measure validity rate and post-parse success.
4) Cost/throughput baseline (C1): same prompt mix across models to compare tokens-per-dollar and effective throughput under autoscaling.

Attachments: I attached a short one-pager comparing feature gaps vs the hyperscalers and a sample prompt suite.

Asks / next steps:
- Can you confirm which three flows you want included in T1? (ticket create, user-lookup, pricing-check are good starting points)
- Do you have sample schema(s) for J1 we can use, or should we start with the examples in the attached CSV?
- Target week for running tests? We have availability to start lightweight tests the week of Oct 5.

I'll loop Camila on the hands-on test execution and Markus for any exec-level questions. Monica can handle procurement hit if you want sandbox credits.

Thanks — Aditya

Sara — great, thanks for the clarifications. Short answers to your two parity questions, plus logistics.

1) Typed function schemas & deterministic ordering:
- Redwood supports typed function definitions (name, typed args, required fields) and returns a structured function call object. Argument ordering is preserved on the call object we deliver to your tool runner; we also provide a canonical serialized form (JSON with predictable key ordering) so downstream systems don't rely on unordered maps.

2) Streaming semantics & chunk ordering:
- Our streaming implementation uses SSE framing with sequence markers. We guarantee in-order delivery per connection; if a client reconnects we provide a small resume token for the KV cache so you can request missing segments. Under high-burst concurrency we prefer short-lived shards and precise reconnect logic vs buffering huge per-connection queues — this is what avoids long p99 tails in our internal tests.

Logistics and schedule:
- Oct 5–7 for baseline streaming & cost (S1 + C1).
- Oct 12–14 for tool/function-calling (T1) + structured outputs (J1).
- We'll provide sandbox credentials and a test harness (curl examples and a small NodeJS runner). Camila will own the runbook and measurements; Monica will provision credits and help with any contract questions.

Camila — can you prepare the sandbox + runbook this week? I attached a short timeline (acme-test-plan-templates.xlsx).

Monica — assuming we run the sandbox with standard trial contract, can your team confirm any procurement blockers (NDA, SOC 2 evidence)?

Thanks — looking forward to running the tests.

Aditya
